chapter: Night life, Guy Kelly and Chicago youth
title: Lawrence Trotter, drinking habits and white friends
summary: He talks of Trotter, drinking in the old days, and having more white friends than colored.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I was talking to Lawrence Trotter on the telephone and he said, you know, he was telling me about how you had a reputation and on the boats and all that.

Yeah, Lawrence Trotter, he was a nice fellow, yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I played with him too, he played with me, yeah. Lawrence Trotter, yeah. Where was that? Well, different gigs, you know, we'd get jump ups, we played some projects down there, on the cycle, the third floor, I mean, and the charity hospital, different groups and things like that.

Well, he told me that at those times, anybody could just walk the streets and, like he'd say, you'd see Earl Millett and he'd be drunk and pass out and people would take his wallet and not take his money and just, you know, give it back to him the next day.

Well you see, he lost a lot of music for me too. And you see, around Chinatown we had one of the best little bands in the city, you see, and people admired us. But like I told you, there wasn't no, why the fool with them weeds or nothing like that. He used to say, I always used to fool them, but I never had seen them. You understand? But see, like beer, that's what oil drank. You understand? Well I drank everything come along, you understand, at that time. Well I drank my olive oil, I wouldn't get drunk. Oh I see.

Yeah, I drank it, as long as I didn't eat that olive oil, it would lick a float up on it. Never did that? It wouldn't burn your line in your stone house. You see, them guys wouldn't eat and everything like spooking them, they wouldn't eat, but I ate. Me, I always kept me a hunk of bologna, I said something like that. I'm very sorry about drinking now, but I mean, when I drank, I used to drink. You see, because the Maracas, a lot of them had died out, well all the uncles, they all had established them all up and down there for Red Street and where they had a place at, they would hire my men, you know, give them a boost like an advertisement, you know, to come in there and line them out. See I had, it was, it wasn't no integration then, but I had more white friends than I had colored, you understand what I mean? Because why is it responsible for me knowing how to play with them? You understand? The little Rockers in them give me the place, Don Tape and all the handsome ones. You see, and after Willie Foster left, I was advancing Mr. Boye-to, he helped me, Philip Boye-to, he helped me, you know.
